manifest.name: dsh-fa-rtl
manifest.description: Right-to-left display for Persian chat messages in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, using per-block bidi auto-detection (CSS unicode-bidi: plaintext).

bundle.text:
# dsh-fa-rtl — bundle patch.
#
# This file is applied when the package is installed and enabled as a bundle
# in a DSH profile (Web "Plugins" page, `dsh plugin add …`, or the
# plugin_manager tool). It registers the single Loader row that mounts the
# plugin; the row name is this package's npm name, resolved from the
# profile's node_modules after installation.
#
# DSH bundle-patch convention: a patch row replaces the targeted row's whole
# config, so every row must restate each key it owns.
- insert:
    - id: fa-rtl
      name: dsh-fa-rtl

readme.text:
**Right-to-left display for Persian (Farsi) chat messages in the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.**

[فارسی](README.fa.md) | English

Persian answers from the model — and your own Persian messages — render right-to-left and right-aligned, while English paragraphs, code blocks, and tables keep their original left-to-right layout. It is a pure DSH plugin: no modification to the application's files, no build toolchain, nothing to configure after install.

`unicode-bidi: plaintext` (CSS Writing Modes 4) lets **each text block** choose its own direction from the block's first strong character — a paragraph starting with Persian renders RTL and right-aligns; a paragraph starting with English is unchanged. Consequences:

- Mixed answers (Persian prose + code + tables) render correctly: prose RTL, `<pre>` code deliberately untouched (stays LTR), table cells per-cell, list markers flip with their list.
- The selector scopes only to stable `data-*` attributes that `dsh-client-ui-chat` emits on its flow items (`data-chat-flow-kind`, `data-chat-group-part`, `data-turn-process-answer`). Build-time hashed class names are never referenced, so the plugin survives UI updates. If an attribute ever changes, the CSS simply stops matching — it cannot break the app.
Requires DSH ≥ 0.2.0-rc.2 with a web composition (`desktop` or `web` profile). Any Chromium/Electron ≥ 105 works.

Open the **Plugins** page in the sidebar and install the bundle from this repository's GitHub address (`github:mehdinikzad68/dsh-fa-rtl`). Installation runs `pnpm` in the profile directory and enables the bundle by default.

dsh plugin --profile web add github:<owner>/dsh-fa-rtl
```

Installation normally enables the bundle automatically; if not, toggle it on from the Plugins page. Restart the app once if your profile applies patches only at startup.
Ask the agent to use the `plugin_manager` tool with action `install_bundle` and the GitHub spec. Each management call requires your approval.

Clone the repo and point a profile patch row at the **module file** (ESM cannot import a directory). In `<profile-dir>/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: fa-rtl
      name: 'C:\path\to\dsh-fa-rtl\lib\index.js'
```

1. Ask the model something in Persian — the Persian text renders RTL and right-aligned; numbers and punctuation sit correctly; code stays LTR.
2. Browser console (or DevTools) shows: `[dsh-fa-rtl] active — Persian chat text now renders right-to-left`
3. `<head>` contains a `<style data-plugin="dsh-fa-rtl">` tag.
4. Settings → Plugins shows no synchronization error for the bundle.

Remove the bundle from the Plugins page or with `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-fa-rtl` (installed route), or delete the `fa-rtl` insert block from `cordis.patch.yml` (local route). The module system removes the plugin's stylesheet when the entry is disabled.

```
dsh-fa-rtl/
├── package.json        # manifest: dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client declaration
├── cordis.patch.yml    # bundle patch: registers the fa-rtl Loader row on install
├── lib/index.js        # Host half (Node): imports cleanly, mounts as a Cordis plugin

- Want more surfaces RTL (e.g. `ask_user_question` cards)? Widen the scope selector list in [`lib/client.js`](lib/client.js) and save — HMR hot-swaps the bundle, or restart once.
- Want *forced* RTL for everything (even English text)? Replace `unicode-bidi: plaintext` with `direction: rtl` in the same file.

- A paragraph that *starts* with a Latin word (e.g. «VS Code را نصب کن») resolves LTR in auto mode — the same behavior as `dir="auto"` everywhere on the web; the Persian runs inside still order correctly.
- Overflowing wide tables keep their physical margins; very wide Persian tables may align slightly differently.
- Question cards (`ask_user_question`) and some side bars are intentionally out of scope for v1.
